cited.quote: Value Rationalization Committee’ vide G.O.(Ms) No.180, Commercial Taxes and Registration Department, dated 27.12.2021.

rationale: C2 reports a GO (No.180, dated 27.12.2021) constituting a Guideline Value Rationalization Committee to rectify anomalies and fix correct guideline values. This is a dedicated official measure on fair guideline values; the directional promise is met.

cited.quote: Excavation of a new Supply Canal from LS 15.950 Km of Barur Tank East Main Canal

rationale: C4 sanctions a supply canal from Barur Tank to feed 33 tanks in Krishnagiri district, but it concerns a different lake system. C1, C2, C3 and C5 cover other links. No extract shows an official step linking the named lake to surrounding lakes.

No extract shows any urging of the Union government to extend a scheme to municipalities. C1 to C5 cover state finance, a state urban scheme, posts and planning areas, none of them an advocacy step on this issue.

cited.quote: statue honouring Veteran Kuyili, a staunch supporter of freedom fighter Veeramangai Velunachiyar
Providing Statue for Freedom Fighter Kuyili at Sivagangai in Sivagangai District

rationale: C1 reports the Kuyili statue in Sivagangai at Rs.50 lakh is nearing completion, and C3 lists it as a Public Works item. Construction is under way but the statue is not reported installed or unveiled, and no GO date is given.

cited.quote: submitted a Memorandum to the Hon’ble Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying on 01.04.2022
immediate release of the remaining fishermen and their crafts, and to find a permanent solution to this issue

rationale: The extracts show the state pressing the Union on Sri Lankan Navy arrests: CM letters and a Minister's memorandum (C2, 01.04.2022), and a call for a permanent solution (C3). They concern fishermen, not farmers as worded, which is a doubt about scope.

cited.quote: In the financial year 2022-2023, 113 temples are being renovated and protected

rationale: C1 reports Rs.100 crore a year for restoring ancient temples, with 113 temples renovated in 2022-23 and 84 in 2023-24. Renovation of ancient temples is under way as promised. Only the financial year is given, not a GO date, so the date is year-level.

cited.quote: the draft notification of New Comprehensive Mini Bus Scheme, 2024 was published in the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette No.190,

rationale: C2 says a new minibus policy was announced and a draft New Comprehensive Mini Bus Scheme, 2024 was gazetted on 14.06.2024 for objections after the 2011 scheme was set aside. This is a draft notification, not an operational scheme.

cited.quote: Memorial Hall construction works are in progress in Namakkal town at an estimated cost of Rs.2,50,00,000/-
Administrative sanction Orders have been issued for installing a statue in Chennai and for constructing an Arangam in Namakkal

rationale: C5 reports administrative sanction orders (2022) for an arangam in Namakkal District for Dr. Subbarayan. C4 (2025) says the Namakkal memorial hall works are in progress at Rs.2.5 crore. Official steps taken, but no completion or opening is shown.

cited.quote: basis, since 2023. For retired temple servants Pongal ex-gratia of Rs.1000/- is given.
An ex-gratia of Rs. 1000/- was given for the retired temple employees.

rationale: C1 and C2 show a Pongal ex-gratia of Rs.1000 given to retired temple employees, which covers the bonus part. No extract shows retired temple employees' pension raised to Rs.5000. The date rests on C1's 'since 2023', which sits next to this sentence, so it is uncertain.

C1 mentions online electricity bill payment and smart metering, the opposite direction to the promise. No extract shows any GO or step discontinuing existing payment methods in favour of payment to the meter-reading official. C2 to C5 are unrelated.

cited.quote: subject to a maximum of 4,000 litres per craft per year to motorized country crafts

rationale: C1 describes existing tax-exempt diesel and subsidised kerosene for fishing crafts, with no increase from 300 to 400 litres. C2 and C3 cover fuel outlets and engine subsidies. No extract shows an order raising the fuel quantity.

cited.quote: Revised Administrative Sanction has been accorded for an amount of Rs.1060.76 crore on 02.03.2024.
Revised Administrative Sanction has been accorded for an amount of Rs.933.23 crore.

rationale: C2 and C3 show a revised administrative sanction for the Thamirabarani-Karumeniyar-Nambiyar link, raised to Rs.1060.76 crore on 02.03.2024, with stages complete and about 99% of land acquired. Earlier revised sanction (C2) is undated, so the only datable step is C3's.

No extract concerns permanent employment for long-serving ad hoc or contract workers in public entities. C1 and C2 are about contract labour rules and registration, and C3 to C5 are bonus orders. None is about regularisation.

cited.quote: The Agricultural College and Research Institute, Madurai was established in 1965.

rationale: C1 notes the existing Madurai agricultural college (1965) within TNAU. C2 to C5 are TNAU programme and policy orders. No extract shows a GO, bill or step to establish a new agricultural university in Madurai.

No extract is about moving Education from the Concurrent List to the State List. C1 to C5 cover degree equivalence, school administration posts, an audit report, a growth fund and backward-class welfare.

cited.quote: Sholingur arrangement to provide a rope car facility is nearing completion

rationale: C2 says a rope car at Sholingur is nearing completion and feasibility reports were obtained for Thiruneermalai and others. These are preparatory or unfinished steps, not an operating facility. Thiruthani, Trichy and Tiruchengodu are not mentioned. C1, C3, C4 and C5 are unrelated.

cited.quote: The following promotions, transfers and postings are ordered with immediate effect
Transfers and Postings of IPS and non IPS officers

rationale: C3 (02.06.2021), C2 (05.06.2021) and C5 are Home Department police notes ordering IPS postings and transfers after the government took office. No extract shows a comparable IAS reshuffle, so only the IPS part is evidenced.

cited.quote: have contributed to a consistent Immunization coverage of over 99% in the State

rationale: C2 and C3 describe the existing Universal Immunization Programme and Mission Indradhanush with high coverage. C4 only revives posts and C5 states 100% immunization as a guideline. No extract shows a new official step to expand the programme.

cited.quote: 46 Cyber Crime Police Stations (CCPS) were constituted with 1 Cyber Crime Police Station for each District
54 Cyber Crime Police Stations (CCPS) are functioning in Tamil Nadu.
the State Cyber Crime Investigation Centre at the Cyber Crime Wing Headquarters, Chennai shall be a Police Station

rationale: C2 and C3 show cyber police stations for every district, including one for crimes against women and children. C2 says FIRs began in April 2021, before office, so it is not dated for this government. C4 (18.02.2022) is the earliest dated GO in the extracts. The date is uncertain.

cited.quote: decided to implement the Price Support Scheme (PSS) for procurement of Copra in Tamil Nadu

rationale: C1 (GO 21, 21.01.2022) implements the copra Price Support Scheme in Tamil Nadu through NAFED, with the Agricultural Marketing Board as the procurement agency; C3, C4 and C2 repeat it for later years. This is a dedicated measure for direct copra procurement, though not through the Coconut Welfare Board.
